parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian ре́тѧзь (rétjazʹ, “chain”), from Old East Slavic ретѧзь (retęzĭ, “chain”), from Proto-Slavic *retędzь, from Proto-Germanic *rakentǭ, from Proto-Indo-European *reǵ- (“to bind”).

parole.significato: cereal, crops or cultures (rye, wheat, etc.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Ukrainian хлѣбъ (xlib), from Old East Slavic хлѣбъ (xlěbŭ), from Proto-Slavic *xlěbъ, from Proto-Germanic *hlaibaz. Compare Gothic 𐌷𐌻𐌰𐌹𐍆𐍃 (hlaifs).

From Old East Slavic художьникъ (xudožĭnikŭ, “artist, painter, master”), from худогъ (xudogŭ, “skillful, knacky; experienced; versed, adept, conversant; lucky”). Hypotetically, this unused adjective in Ukrainian would be *худо́жий; from Proto-Slavic *xǫdogъ, from a reflex of Proto-Germanic *handuz.
